did_you_know.text: Did you know? After Joshua’s death, the Israelites asked the Lord who should lead the war against the Canaanites. The Lord replied that Judah should go first.
Did you know? Judah invited Simeon, his brother, to join him in the war, and the two tribes acted together: Judah in Simeon’s territory and Simeon in Judah’s territory.
Did you know? Adoni-bezek said that seventy kings whose thumbs and big toes had been cut off used to gather scraps under his table, and he saw his punishment as repayment for his deeds.
Did you know? The people of Judah captured Jerusalem and set the city on fire, yet later in the chapter it says that the Benjamites did not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem.
Did you know? Caleb offered his daughter Achsah in marriage to whoever captured Kiriath-sepher, and Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, captured the city.
Did you know? Achsah asked her father Caleb for a field and springs of water, and Caleb gave her the Upper and Lower Springs.
Did you know? The Kenites, mentioned as descendants of Moses’ father-in-law, went up with the people of Judah and settled in the wilderness of Judah, in the Negev near Arad.
Did you know? Judah succeeded in driving out the inhabitants of the hill country, but not those of the plain, because the inhabitants of the plain had iron chariots.
Did you know? The man from Bethel who helped the house of Joseph found a new place in the land of the Hittites, built a city there, and named it Luz—the same name as the city he had left.
Did you know? Many tribes did not drive out all the inhabitants of the land. At times they subdued the Canaanites and forced them to pay tribute, but the Canaanites continued to live among them.
